evals.name: query-ownership-and-defaults
evals.prompt: At Arc.Kotlin 7.7.0, TaskView.byStatus has status: String = "open" and a repository dependency. Explain the Kotlin method placement and parameter annotations, the equivalent Java placement, and omitted versus explicitly null caller arguments. Can I overload byStatus? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Use a public companion query with FromServices on the repository, or a Java static query. Omission invokes the Kotlin default; explicit null is supplied and requires nullability. Query overloads are unsupported.
assertions: Places the Kotlin query on a ReadModel companion object and the Java equivalent on a public static method rather than an instance handler.
Uses FromServices for the repository and keeps the caller status parameter unannotated.
Distinguishes omission from explicit null: only omission runs the Kotlin default, while null requires a nullable parameter.
Refuses overloaded query methods instead of recommending overloads for optional arguments.

evals.name: java-current-observable-state
evals.prompt: Our Java Arc 7.7.0 query returns a SubmissionPublisher<List<TaskView>>. No update has occurred and snapshot GET keeps returning 202. Explain a current-state source for Java, the Kotlin equivalent, and the observable transports. Do not assume the .NET Subject discovery rules apply. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: SubmissionPublisher holds no current value. ObservableState is a Flow.Publisher with current-first/latest-state behavior; Kotlin uses StateFlow. Streaming return families are discovered automatically and support snapshot, SSE and WebSocket routes.
assertions: Explains why a plain SubmissionPublisher supplies no initial snapshot and recommends ObservableState initialized with the current list.
Identifies ObservableState as a JDK Flow.Publisher, with current-first delivery and latest-value conflation rather than a discrete-event backlog.
Uses MutableStateFlow exposed as Flow for the Kotlin equivalent instead of recommending the Java helper unnecessarily.
Distinguishes snapshot HTTP from SSE and WebSocket and does not import .NET's Subject discovery restriction into the JVM streaming families.

evals.name: provider-owned-page
evals.prompt: At Arc.Kotlin 7.7.0, our custom QueryRendererFor already sorts and pages task results. We want Arc to append another implicit paging stage. Is that correct? Describe QueryPage, the no-paging/no-sort values, and how a query chooses GET or QUERY. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: The application renderer chain owns sorting/paging; no implicit extra stage follows it. Return QueryPage or explicitly include QueryableQueryRenderer. QueryPage carries zero-based page, pageSize and Long totalItems. HTTP-method metadata chooses GET/QUERY/AUTO.
assertions: Rejects implicit additional paging after a matching application QueryRendererFor chain and suggests QueryPage or an explicit QueryableQueryRenderer stage.
Describes QueryPage(items, page, pageSize, totalItems) with zero-based page and Long totalItems, not a nonexistent Arc Page type.
Names QueryPaging.UNPAGED and QuerySorting.UNSORTED for absent paging/sorting.
Distinguishes GET scalar query strings from QUERY's structured arguments/paging/sorting body and identifies QueryHttpMethod metadata with class defaults and method overrides.
